# The question

The same question as the hard report asks, with soft topics: which topics
does the judge-steered Markov walk (the chains from far-apart starts under
the judge Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, as described there) put into the
seventeen lost
verses of P.Oxy. 5292 (vv. 13–29), and does that differ from what Sophocles
writes elsewhere? Here a lemma belongs to every topic with some
probability, so the posterior over a document's topic profile has no closed
form; it is sampled exactly, document by document, with Stan. The sections
follow the hard report one by one, so that the two can be read side by side.

# The model

A document is one whole restoration of the seventeen lost verses: its $N$
content lemmata, however many there are, drawn from the mixture
$\sum_k \theta_k \phi_k$ with $\theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha)$. The
topic-word distributions $\phi$ ($K \times V$) are **soft**: a lemma has
probability under several topics, so every word is a mixture and the
posterior $p(\theta \mid \text{document})$ has no closed form. The model is
fitted in two stages, and the second never feeds back into the first (a
*cut* model in Plummer's sense, 2015): nothing of Sophocles or of the
restorations reaches $\phi$, so the baseline is a test corpus like the
restorations and $\phi$ is not fitted on the text it is then compared with.

**Stage one** is a seeded latent Dirichlet allocation (tomotopy, collapsed
Gibbs sampling) on the windows of Aeschylus and Euripides. Each of the
unsupervised clusters of the hard model seeds one topic with a strong word
prior on all its lemmata, and four free topics are fitted without seeds.
The LDA also estimates its own $\alpha$, one concentration per topic, by
maximising the marginal likelihood every ten sweeps (the empirical Bayes
of the usual LDA implementations), and that vector is the prior on $\theta$
in stage two: $\phi$ and $\alpha$ are then the pair under which the tragedy
corpus was fitted, not $\phi$ with a prior chosen by hand; the last section
sets three hand-chosen priors beside it. The sampler runs single-threaded
from a fixed seed, so the fit reproduces, for 10,000 sweeps of burn-in,
after which twenty states of the chain, 500 sweeps apart, are kept:
$(\phi_j, \alpha_j)$ for $j = 1, \dots, 20$. The report's $\phi$ is thus not
one Gibbs state but twenty, and what moves between them is the uncertainty
in $\phi$ that a single state would hide. What they cannot show is another
mode of the LDA, since all twenty come from one chain with the same seeds.

**Stage two** samples every document's $\theta$ exactly, given one state,
with Stan, and does so once per state; the posterior reported is the mixture

$$p(\theta \mid w_{1:N}) \approx \frac{1}{20} \sum_{j=1}^{20}
  p(\theta \mid w_{1:N}, \phi_j, \alpha_j),$$

and every interval below pools the draws of the twenty states.

The documents are those of the hard report: the imputations, one document per
untilted snapshot, and Sophocles' extant trimeters in windows of seventeen,
the baseline. The imputations are read on two levels: their **mean
profile**, the documents' posteriors averaged draw by draw, compared with
Sophocles' by
$P(\bar\theta_k^{\text{imp}} > \bar\theta_k^{\text{Soph}})$ and the lift
of the means, and a **random document** against a random window,
$P(\theta_k^{\text{doc}} > \theta_k^{\text{window}})$. A topic is **raised**
when the whole 90 % interval of its lift lies above 1, that is, when the
posterior puts at least 95 % of its mass on the imputations' mean share
exceeding Sophocles'. A threshold on the lift itself would be a statement
relative to the prior, as the section on the prior shows.

**Sampling.** With $\phi$ and $\alpha$ fixed, the posterior of one document
is the density on the simplex

$$p(\theta \mid w_{1:N}) \propto \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\theta \mid \alpha)
  \prod_{n=1}^{N} \sum_{k=1}^{K} \theta_k\, \phi_{k w_n},$$

$K - 1 = 37$ free dimensions and at most 58 terms, which Stan's NUTS samples
exactly in some seconds. The program is `lda_given_phi.stan`:

```{r stan_program, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines("lda_given_phi.stan"), sep = "\n")
```

The learned $\alpha$ is below 1 on every seeded topic, and a Dirichlet
density with $\alpha_k < 1$ is unbounded at the corners of the simplex,
where $\theta_k \to 0$. At Stan's default target acceptance of 0.8 nearly
every document showed divergent transitions. The usual remedies were tried
on a handful of documents, sampling $\theta$ through independent gamma
variates and a dense mass matrix, and neither bought anything over the plain
simplex once the target acceptance was raised to 0.99, which is what the
runs use, at the price of a smaller step size and more leapfrog steps per
draw. Every document of every set is sampled with four chains of 500 warmup
and 1,000 sampling iterations, by one CmdStan process per core of a GH200
node, once per state (`scripts/soft_model.py`, `slurm/soft_draws.slurm`, an
array of twenty tasks of about two hours each); 100 draws of each document
are kept per state, and Stan's diagnostics for every fit, the split
$\hat R$, the bulk effective sample size, divergent transitions and
tree-depth hits, are recorded. `scripts/soft_pool.py` pools the twenty runs
into the files this report reads. The posterior is exact up to Monte Carlo
error, so there is nothing to calibrate: the checks are the diagnostics.

# Data

The GPU scripts read the same dataset as the hard report
(`Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026`: the bags of content lemmata, the
vocabulary with its cluster labels, the corpus of the three tragedians, the
baseline windows). Stage one writes to `results/soft/lda/` the twenty states
of $\phi$ and $\alpha$ (`phi_draws.npz`, kept in the dataset's `soft/`
folder, not in the repository) and the mean of the states with its top
lemmata and the mean $\alpha$ (`phi.json`, `phi_matrix.csv.gz`). Stage two
writes one folder per state, `results/soft/draws/d00` to `d19`, and
`scripts/soft_pool.py` pools them into `results/soft/pooled/`, which this
report reads: the diagnostics of every document, the worst over the states
(`diagnostics.csv.gz`), and the counts per state
(`diagnostics_by_draw.csv`); two documents with their posterior summary for
the refit below (`check_documents.json`, from the first state); the mean
profiles of the four sets of documents, the imputations, Sophocles and the
two further baselines, with the imputations' lift (`profiles.csv`); and the
comparisons between the sets with intervals of three kinds
(`comparisons.csv`, with every lift at every single state in
`lifts_by_state.csv`). The four runs of the prior check
(`results/soft/mean_alpha_*`) hold the same files under the mean $\phi$.
This document downloads the two phi files into the results folder when they
are absent, and stops here, with a note, if the run has not been made yet.

```{r load, include = FALSE}
hub <- "https://huggingface.co/datasets/Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026"
fetch <- function(file_name, remote, local_path) {
  url <- paste(c(hub, "resolve/main", remote, file_name), collapse = "/")
  try(download.file(url, local_path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE))
}
fetch_phi <- function() {
  for (file_name in c("phi.json", "phi_matrix.csv.gz")) {
    fetch(file_name, "soft", file.path(results_dir, file_name))
  }
}
if (dir.exists(results_dir) &&
    !file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "phi_matrix.csv.gz"))) {
  fetch_phi()
}
# A phi left over from an earlier run (the vocabulary has changed since)
# is caught by its vocabulary size and replaced by the dataset's copy
dir.create(params$data, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
vocab_path <- file.path(params$data, "vocab.json")
if (!file.exists(vocab_path)) fetch("vocab.json", NULL, vocab_path)
V <- nrow(fromJSON(vocab_path))
phi_path <- file.path(results_dir, "phi.json")
if (file.exists(phi_path) && fromJSON(phi_path)$vocab_size != V) {
  fetch_phi()
}
needed <- c("phi.json", "phi_matrix.csv.gz", "diagnostics.csv.gz",
            "diagnostics_by_draw.csv", "check_documents.json", "profiles.csv",
            "comparisons.csv", "lifts_by_state.csv", "pooled.json")
missing <- needed[!file.exists(file.path(results_dir, needed))]
if (length(missing) == 0 && fromJSON(phi_path)$vocab_size != V) {
  cat("The phi in", results_dir, "is from another vocabulary (",
      fromJSON(phi_path)$vocab_size, "lemmata, the dataset has", V,
      ") and the dataset's copy could not be fetched.\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  cat("The soft model's run has not been made yet: missing",
      paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
phi <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "phi.json"))
profiles <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "profiles.csv"),
                     encoding = "UTF-8")
diagnostics <- read.csv(gzfile(file.path(results_dir, "diagnostics.csv.gz")))
comparisons <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "comparisons.csv"),
                        encoding = "UTF-8")
by_state <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "diagnostics_by_draw.csv"))
lifts_by_state <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "lifts_by_state.csv"),
                           encoding = "UTF-8")
pooled <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "pooled.json"))

phi_matrix <- read.csv(gzfile(file.path(results_dir, "phi_matrix.csv.gz")),
                       row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE,
                       encoding = "UTF-8")
phi_matrix <- as.matrix(phi_matrix)                  # K topics by V lemmata
topic_names <- phi$names
K <- length(topic_names)                          # seeded + free topics
H <- sum(profiles$source == "sophocles")          # seeded topics only
profiles$source <- factor(profiles$source,
                          levels = c("imputations", "sophocles", "tragedians",
                                     "attic"))
imputations <- filter(profiles, source == "imputations")

figure <- function(paths) {
  drawn <- paths[file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(drawn) == 0) {
    cat("(figure not drawn yet:", paste(paths, collapse = ", "), ")")
  } else {
    knitr::include_graphics(drawn)
  }
}
```

`r H` seeded topics and `r K - H` free topics on a vocabulary of
`r phi$vocab_size` lemmata; the LDA's log-likelihood per word is
`r round(phi$ll_per_word, 3)` at the last state, and `r pooled$states`
states were kept. The learned $\alpha$, averaged over the states, runs from
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(phi$alpha[1:H]))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(phi$alpha[1:H]))` on the seeded topics and from
`r sprintf("%.1f", min(phi$alpha[-(1:H)]))` to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(phi$alpha[-(1:H)]))` on the free ones, and sums to
`r sprintf("%.1f", sum(phi$alpha))`: the prior alone gives the four free
topics `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * sum(phi$alpha[-(1:H)]) / sum(phi$alpha))` %
of a document.

# The topics

The ten top lemmata of every topic as the seeded LDA fitted them on
Aeschylus and Euripides (the mean of the twenty states), with the number of
seed lemmata found in the vocabulary and the topic's learned $\alpha_k$.

```{r topics, results = "asis"}
for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  topic <- topic_names[k]
  top_words <- paste(head(phi$top_words[[topic]], 10), collapse = " ")
  if (k <= H) {
    n_seeds <- length(phi$seeds_found[[topic]])
    cat("- **", topic, "** (", n_seeds, " seeds, $\\alpha_k$ = ",
        sprintf("%.2f", phi$alpha[k]), "): ", top_words, "\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("- **", topic, "** (free, $\\alpha_k$ = ",
        sprintf("%.1f", phi$alpha[k]), "): ", top_words, "\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

What soft topics buy: a word can belong elsewhere than its cluster put it.
For every lemma, $\phi_{k,w}$ normalised over the topics is the probability
of topic $k$ given the word (a flat prior over topics); where the most
probable topic is not the lemma's cluster, the lemma has moved. The first
table counts the movers by the topic they move to, free topics marked; the
second lists the movers the tragedians use most, with the probability of
the cluster and of the new topic.

```{r moved_lemmata}
vocab <- fromJSON(vocab_path)
with_topic <- vocab[!is.na(vocab$cluster_K40), ]
responsibility <- phi_matrix[, with_topic$lemma]
responsibility <- sweep(responsibility, 2, colSums(responsibility), "/")
soft_topic <- rownames(phi_matrix)[apply(responsibility, 2, which.max)]
moved <- with_topic$cluster_K40 != soft_topic
to_free <- moved & !(soft_topic %in% topic_names[1:H])
cat(sum(moved), "of", nrow(with_topic), "clustered lemmata move,",
    sum(to_free), "of them to a free topic.\n")
free_mark <- ifelse(soft_topic %in% topic_names[1:H], soft_topic,
                    paste(soft_topic, "(free)"))
movers <- data.frame(lemma = with_topic$lemma,
                     tragic_tokens = with_topic$tragic_count,
                     cluster = with_topic$cluster_K40,
                     p_cluster = responsibility[cbind(
                       match(with_topic$cluster_K40, rownames(phi_matrix)),
                       seq_len(nrow(with_topic)))],
                     soft_topic = free_mark,
                     p_soft = apply(responsibility, 2, max))[moved, ]
destinations <- movers %>%
  group_by(soft_topic) %>%
  summarise(lemmata = n(), tragic_tokens = sum(tragic_tokens)) %>%
  arrange(desc(tragic_tokens))
knitr::kable(destinations, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Where the movers go: lemmata and tragic tokens")
movers <- head(arrange(movers, desc(tragic_tokens)), 30)
knitr::kable(movers, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The thirty most frequent lemmata that move")
```

# The posterior

Stan's diagnostics over every document that was sampled, twenty times each,
once per state. The first table counts, within a state and for each set,
the documents whose fit had a split $\hat R$ above 1.01 for any topic, a
bulk effective sample size under 400 for any topic (of 4,000 draws), any
divergent transition or any tree-depth hit, as the median and the largest
count over the twenty states, with the worst values seen and the median
time per document. The second counts a document once if any of its twenty
fits was flagged, so it is the stricter of the two.

```{r diagnostics_by_state}
state_counts <- by_state %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(documents = first(documents),
            rhat_over_1.01 = sprintf("%.0f to %d", median(rhat_over_1_01),
                                     max(rhat_over_1_01)),
            ess_under_400 = sprintf("%.0f to %d", median(ess_under_400),
                                    max(ess_under_400)),
            divergent = sprintf("%.0f to %d", median(divergent),
                                max(divergent)),
            treedepth = sprintf("%.0f to %d", median(treedepth),
                                max(treedepth)),
            worst_rhat = max(worst_rhat),
            least_ess = min(least_ess),
            seconds = median(seconds))
knitr::kable(state_counts, digits = 3,
             caption = paste("Stan's diagnostics within a state: the median",
                             "to the largest count over the twenty states"))
```

```{r diagnostics}
diagnostics_table <- diagnostics %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(documents = n(),
            rhat_over_1.01 = sum(max_rhat > 1.01),
            ess_under_400 = sum(min_ess_bulk < 400),
            divergent = sum(divergences > 0),
            treedepth = sum(treedepth_hits > 0),
            worst_rhat = max(max_rhat),
            least_ess = min(min_ess_bulk))
knitr::kable(diagnostics_table, digits = 3,
             caption = paste("The same, a document counted once if flagged",
                             "at any state"))
```

Under the learned prior the sampler has a harder time than under a flat
one, and the section on the prior shows the same documents sampled without
a single flag under $\mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1)$. A seeded topic with
an $\alpha_k$ of 0.1 or 0.2 is, in a document that does not use it,
posterior mass piled against $\theta_k = 0$ with a thin tail; a chain that
strays into the tail for a while shows up as an $\hat R$ above 1.01 and a
small effective sample size for that topic, in about a tenth of the
documents at any one state. The tree-depth hits are the price of the target
acceptance of 0.99: a small step size exhausts the ten doublings of NUTS's
trajectory in some documents, which costs time but, unlike a divergence,
does not bias the draw. What the report uses is the mean profile over
hundreds or thousands of documents, in which the Monte Carlo error of one
document's mean is averaged away; the agreement between the twenty states,
each a separate run, in the section on the intervals below is the check on
that.

The same diagnostics as bayesplot draws them, one value per document at
its worst state: its largest $\hat R$ over the topics, and its smallest
bulk effective sample size as a share of the 4,000 draws.

```{r diagnostics_plot, fig.height = 2.6}
mcmc_rhat_hist(diagnostics$max_rhat) +
  labs(title = paste("Largest split R-hat over the topics and states,",
                     "one per document"))
mcmc_neff_hist(diagnostics$min_ess_bulk / 4000) +
  labs(title = paste("Smallest bulk ESS over the topics and states,",
                     "one per document"))
```

## Two documents refitted here

One snapshot of the imputations and one window of Sophocles, drawn at random by
the GPU script, are sampled again here with `rstan` from the same program,
the same $\phi$ and the same $\alpha$, those of the first state (the GPU
script stores the document's rows of $\log \phi$ and the prior beside its
summary), so that the chains can be looked at, and the stored summary (from
100 kept draws) is set beside the fresh one (from
`r 4 * params$check_iter / 2` draws).

```{r check_model}
check_model <- stan_model("lda_given_phi.stan")
check_set <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "check_documents.json"),
                      simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

```{r check_fits, results = "asis", fig.height = 3.5}
check_alpha <- unlist(check_set$alpha)
if (is.null(check_alpha)) check_alpha <- rep(1, K)   # runs before the prior
for (document in check_set$documents) {
  lemmata <- unlist(document$lemma_idx) + 1          # R counts from 1
  if (is.null(document$logphi)) {                    # runs before it was stored
    logphi <- t(log(phi_matrix[, lemmata]))
  } else {
    logphi <- do.call(rbind, lapply(document$logphi, unlist))
  }
  stan_data <- list(N = length(lemmata), K = K, alpha = check_alpha,
                    logphi = logphi)
  fit <- sampling(check_model, data = stan_data, chains = 4,
                  iter = params$check_iter, warmup = params$check_iter / 2,
                  refresh = 0, seed = 917,
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
  fit_summary <- summary(fit, pars = "theta")$summary
  stored_mean <- unlist(document$mean)
  largest <- order(stored_mean, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]
  side_by_side <- data.frame(topic = topic_names[largest],
                             stored_mean = stored_mean[largest],
                             stored_sd = unlist(document$sd)[largest],
                             mean = fit_summary[largest, "mean"],
                             sd = fit_summary[largest, "sd"],
                             n_eff = fit_summary[largest, "n_eff"],
                             rhat = fit_summary[largest, "Rhat"])
  cat("\n\n**", document$source, "**, document ", document$index,
      " (", length(lemmata), " lemmata): ",
      sum(get_divergent_iterations(fit)), " divergent transitions, ",
      "largest R-hat over all topics ",
      sprintf("%.3f", max(fit_summary[, "Rhat"])), ".\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(side_by_side, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE))
  print(mcmc_trace(fit, pars = paste0("theta[", largest, "]"),
                   facet_args = list(ncol = 5)) +
          labs(title = paste("Chains of the five largest topics,",
                             document$source)) +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
}
```

The four sets of documents: the imputations, Sophocles, and the two further
baselines of the section on them below.

```{r sizes}
sizes <- unique(profiles[, c("source", "n_docs", "n_lemmata")])
knitr::kable(sizes, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Documents, and content lemmata per document")
```

# Sophocles' baseline

Sophocles' mean profile, the seeded topics ordered by their share, each
with its posterior mean and 90 % interval on a log scale, so that the
small differences between topics can be read; the dashed line is the
share every topic would have if all were equal.

```{r baseline, fig.height = 5}
sophocles_rows <- filter(profiles, source == "sophocles")
baseline_table <- data.frame(topic = reorder(sophocles_rows$topic,
                                             sophocles_rows$mean),
                             mean = sophocles_rows$mean,
                             q05 = sophocles_rows$q05,
                             q95 = sophocles_rows$q95)
ggplot(baseline_table, aes(x = mean, y = topic)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1 / K, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = q05, xmax = q95), colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]],
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "posterior mean of theta, with its 90 % interval (log scale)",
       y = NULL,
       title = paste("Sophocles,", sophocles_rows$n_docs[1],
                     "windows of seventeen trimeters"))
```

# Topics raised above Sophocles

Seeded topics whose 90 % interval of the lift lies above 1, with the lift,
its interval, the posterior mean and, in brackets, the document-level
probability.

```{r raised, results = "asis"}
interval <- filter(comparisons, comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
imputations <- inner_join(imputations,
                          interval[, c("topic", "lift_q05", "lift_q95")],
                          by = "topic")
imputations$raised <- imputations$lift_q05 > 1
raised <- arrange(filter(imputations, raised), desc(lift))
if (nrow(raised) == 0) {
  cat("None.\n")
} else {
  items <- sprintf("%s (%.2f×, %.2f to %.2f; mean %.2f [%.2f])",
                   raised$topic, raised$lift, raised$lift_q05,
                   raised$lift_q95, raised$mean, raised$p_document)
  cat(paste(items, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

# Lift of every topic

The lift of every topic, ordered by lift, with its 90 % interval (from
`comparisons.csv`) on a log scale, where a lift of 2 and of 1/2 sit at the
same distance from the dashed line at 1.

```{r lifts, fig.height = 5}
lifts <- imputations
lifts$topic <- reorder(lifts$topic, lifts$lift)
ggplot(lifts, aes(x = lift, y = topic, colour = raised)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lift_q05, xmax = lift_q95),
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey60", okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]),
                      name = "raised: 90 % interval\nabove 1") +
  labs(x = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles (log scale)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# The largest lifts

The five topics with the largest lift.

```{r top}
top_five <- head(arrange(imputations, desc(lift)), 5)
top_five <- top_five[, c("topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "p_above_sophocles",
                         "lift", "p_document")]
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Beyond Sophocles: three baselines

The same two further baselines as in the hard report, Aeschylus and
Euripides and Classical Attic (`data/attic_windows.parquet`, windows of 30
lemmata of the Attic authors before Alexander), every window sampled like
the restorations: the baseline's mean profile is compared with the imputations'
draw by draw, and a lift's 90 % interval is that of the ratio of the two
mean profiles over the posterior draws of the twenty states, focus and
baseline paired within a state; the section after the next adds the
bootstrap. `scripts/soft_circles.py` draws the grids from
`results/soft/pooled/comparisons.csv`. The area of a circle runs from the
smallest mean share to the largest: the shares of 34 topics lie within
a factor of two of each other, and circles proportional to the share
itself would all look alike.

```{r soft_circles_imputations, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
figure(c("figures/soft_circles_imputations_vs_sophocles.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_imputations_vs_tragedians.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_imputations_vs_attic.png"))
```

Sophocles as the focus, against the other two tragedians and against
Classical Attic:

```{r soft_circles_sophocles, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
figure(c("figures/soft_circles_sophocles_vs_tragedians.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_sophocles_vs_attic.png"))
```

```{r soft_baselines_table}
comparisons$off_one <- comparisons$lift_q05 > 1 | comparisons$lift_q95 < 1
baseline_rows <- NULL
for (comparison in unique(comparisons$comparison)) {
  these <- filter(comparisons, comparison == !!comparison, off_one)
  these <- arrange(these, desc(lift))
  largest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", head(these$topic, 3),
                           head(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  smallest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", tail(these$topic, 3),
                            tail(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  baseline_rows <- rbind(baseline_rows,
                         data.frame(comparison = comparison,
                                    off_one = nrow(these),
                                    largest = largest, smallest = smallest))
}
knitr::kable(baseline_rows, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("comparison", "topics off 1", "largest lifts",
                           "smallest lifts"))
```

The two lifts of every topic of the imputations side by side: against Sophocles
(the question of this report) and against Classical Attic (whether the
topic is tragic at all). A topic in the upper right is more frequent in
the imputations than in both; one on the dashed line at 1 is at its baseline's
rate. The dot is the imputations' mean share of the topic, the grey lines the
90 % intervals.

```{r lift_scatter, fig.height = 5.2}
against <- function(baseline) {
  rows <- filter(comparisons, comparison == paste("imputations vs", baseline))
  rows[, c("topic", "rate_focus", "lift", "lift_q05", "lift_q95")]
}
scatter <- inner_join(against("sophocles"), against("attic"),
                      by = c("topic", "rate_focus"),
                      suffix = c("_sophocles", "_attic"))
scatter$off_one <- scatter$lift_q05_sophocles > 1 |
  scatter$lift_q95_sophocles < 1 | scatter$lift_q05_attic > 1 |
  scatter$lift_q95_attic < 1
# every topic is labelled where ggrepel can keep the labels apart; without
# it, only the topics with an interval off 1 (the crowd at 1 stays unnamed)
labels <- if (requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = topic), size = 2,
                           family = figure_font, max.overlaps = Inf,
                           segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey60")
} else {
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(off_one, topic, "")), size = 2,
            vjust = -1.1, family = figure_font)
}
ggplot(scatter, aes(x = lift_attic, y = lift_sophocles)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lift_q05_sophocles, ymax = lift_q95_sophocles),
                 colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lift_q05_attic, xmax = lift_q95_attic),
                 colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(size = rate_focus), colour = okabe_ito[["blue"]],
             alpha = 0.7) +
  labels +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = paste("The soft model: the imputations' lift against Sophocles",
                     "and Classical Attic"),
       x = "lift against Classical Attic (log scale)",
       y = "lift against Sophocles (log scale)",
       size = "mean share")
```

The topics the hard report singles out, *wrong-vengeance-err* and
*god-true-lord*, the two lifts that hold against every baseline there, and

```{r soft_held}
               topic %in% c("wrong-vengeance-err", "god-true-lord",
```

# Which seeded topic dominates

A reading the soft model alone affords, since its posterior is over the
whole simplex at once: for a random document of the imputations, of
Sophocles, of Aeschylus and Euripides or of Classical Attic, the probability
that each
seeded topic is the largest.

```{r dominant, fig.height = 7}
heat <- profiles
heat$topic <- factor(heat$topic, levels = rev(topic_names[1:H]))
ggplot(heat, aes(x = source, y = topic, fill = p_dominant)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = okabe_ito[["blue"]],
                      name = "P(largest\nseeded topic)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Which seeded topic dominates a random document")
```

The five largest mean profiles of Sophocles and of the imputations.

```{r mass}
columns <- c("source", "topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "lift",
             "p_above_sophocles", "p_document")
top_five <- rbind(head(arrange(sophocles_rows, desc(mean)), 5)[, columns],
                  head(arrange(imputations, desc(mean)), 5)[, columns])
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

# What the intervals leave out

The 90 % intervals so far are posterior intervals of the mean profile given
$\phi$: they carry the uncertainty of every document's $\theta$ and, since
the draws of twenty states are pooled, the uncertainty in $\phi$ that the
Gibbs chain shows. Two things remain to be looked at. The first is what a
single state of $\phi$ would have hidden; the second is the dependence
between the restorations, which the posterior treats as independent
documents given $\phi$, although the snapshots of one walk chain share most
of their text.

## Twenty states of phi against one

The lift of every seeded topic against Sophocles: the pooled 90 % interval
(vermillion), the lift at each of the twenty single states (grey dots),
and the interval of the plug-in run under the mean $\phi$ and the mean
$\alpha$ (blue, `results/soft/mean_alpha_lda`), the run that one state
would have given.

```{r phi_plot, fig.height = 5.5}
plugin_dir <- file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_lda")
plugin <- read.csv(file.path(plugin_dir, "comparisons.csv"),
                   encoding = "UTF-8")
plugin <- filter(plugin, comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
pooled_lifts <- filter(comparisons, comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
topic_order <- pooled_lifts$topic[order(pooled_lifts$lift)]
both <- bind_rows(mutate(pooled_lifts, run = "pooled over twenty states"),
                  mutate(plugin, run = "plug-in: mean phi, mean alpha"))
both$topic <- factor(both$topic, levels = topic_order)
state_lifts <- filter(lifts_by_state,
                      comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
state_lifts$topic <- factor(state_lifts$topic, levels = topic_order)
ggplot(both, aes(x = lift, y = topic, colour = run)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = state_lifts, aes(x = lift, y = topic), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             colour = "grey55", size = 0.6, alpha = 0.7,
             position = position_nudge(y = 0.22)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lift_q05, xmax = lift_q95),
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(okabe_ito[["blue"]],
                                 okabe_ito[["vermillion"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles (log scale)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r phi_summary, results = "asis"}
log_width <- function(low, high) log(high / low)
pooled_width <- median(log_width(pooled_lifts$lift_q05, pooled_lifts$lift_q95))
plugin_width <- median(log_width(plugin$lift_q05, plugin$lift_q95))
state_range <- state_lifts %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(low = min(lift), high = max(lift))
state_width <- median(log_width(state_range$low, state_range$high))
off_one <- function(rows) sum(rows$lift_q05 > 1 | rows$lift_q95 < 1)
raised_of <- function(rows) {
  as.character(arrange(filter(rows, lift_q05 > 1), desc(lift))$topic)
}
or_none <- function(topics) {
  if (length(topics) == 0) "none" else paste(topics, collapse = ", ")
}
same_raised <- setequal(raised_of(pooled_lifts), raised_of(plugin))
# in how many of the twenty states each pooled raised topic is raised
states_raised <- state_lifts %>%
  filter(topic %in% raised_of(pooled_lifts)) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(states = sum(lift_q05 > 1), lift = mean(lift)) %>%
  arrange(desc(lift))
top_topic <- pooled_lifts$topic[which.max(pooled_lifts$lift)]
top_range <- filter(state_range, topic == top_topic)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "The lift of %s lies between %.2f and %.2f over the twenty states;",
  "for the median topic the twenty lifts span a factor of %.2f. The median",
  "90 %% interval is a factor of %.2f wide pooled and %.2f under the",
  "plug-in run (%.0f %% wider on the log scale); %d topics have an interval",
  "off 1 pooled, %d under the plug-in run. Raised pooled: %s; under the",
  "plug-in run: %s. Counting the states one at a time, %s.\n"),
  top_topic, top_range$low, top_range$high, exp(state_width),
  exp(pooled_width), exp(plugin_width),
  100 * (pooled_width / plugin_width - 1), off_one(pooled_lifts),
  off_one(plugin), or_none(raised_of(pooled_lifts)),
  or_none(raised_of(plugin)),
  paste(sprintf("%s is raised in %d of the twenty", states_raised$topic,
                states_raised$states), collapse = ", ")))
```

The states agree with each other. The twenty lifts of a topic are spread
over a factor of `r sprintf("%.2f", exp(state_width))` for the median
topic, inside its posterior interval, and pooling the states widens the
median interval by
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (pooled_width / plugin_width - 1))` % on the log
scale against the plug-in run. The raised set is
`r if (same_raised) "the same" else "not the same"` under both, the
point estimates nearly so. The uncertainty in $\phi$ is real and is now in
the intervals, but it is small next to the posterior uncertainty of the
profiles, which the plug-in run already carries. One caveat was stated
above: twenty states of one chain show the spread within a mode of the LDA,
not between modes.

## The dependence between restorations

The imputations are `r imputations$n_docs[1]` snapshots of
`r pooled$chains` chains of the walk, and consecutive snapshots of a chain
differ by a few verses. The posterior of the mean profile shrinks with the
number of documents as if they were independent; the hard report meets this
with a bootstrap by chain, and the same is done here: `r pooled$bootstrap`
replicates, each with the imputations resampled by chain, Sophocles'
windows resampled, a state of $\phi$ drawn at random, and the posterior
noise of the two mean profiles added back (a random draw's deviation from
the mean of its state), so that the bootstrap interval carries everything
the posterior interval does and the dependence on top. With
`r pooled$chains` chains it is a coarse bootstrap, but an honest one. The
plot sets the two intervals side by side, with the probability of the lift
being above 1 under each.

```{r chain_plot, fig.height = 5.5}
chain <- pooled_lifts
chain$topic <- factor(chain$topic, levels = topic_order)
intervals <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(topic = chain$topic, lift = chain$lift, low = chain$lift_q05,
             high = chain$lift_q95, p = chain$p_above,
             kind = "posterior, pooled over the states"),
  data.frame(topic = chain$topic, lift = chain$lift, low = chain$lift_chain_q05,
             high = chain$lift_chain_q95, p = chain$p_chain_above,
             kind = "chain bootstrap"))
intervals$kind <- factor(intervals$kind,
                         levels = c("posterior, pooled over the states",
                                    "chain bootstrap"))
ggplot(intervals, aes(x = lift, y = topic, colour = kind)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 3.2, label = sprintf("%.2f", p)), size = 2,
            family = figure_font, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2), limits = c(0.35, 3.6)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(okabe_ito[["vermillion"]],
                                 okabe_ito[["green"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "lift against Sophocles (log scale); at the right, P(lift > 1)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r chain_summary, results = "asis"}
chain_width <- median(log_width(chain$lift_chain_q05, chain$lift_chain_q95))
off_chain <- sum(chain$lift_chain_q05 > 1 | chain$lift_chain_q95 < 1)
raised_chain <- filter(chain, lift_chain_q05 > 1)
raised_chain <- as.character(arrange(raised_chain, desc(lift))$topic)
# the topics the two intervals disagree on: off 1 under one, covering 1
# under the other
posterior_off <- chain$lift_q05 > 1 | chain$lift_q95 < 1
bootstrap_off <- chain$lift_chain_q05 > 1 | chain$lift_chain_q95 < 1
lost <- as.character(chain$topic[posterior_off & !bootstrap_off])
gained <- as.character(chain$topic[!posterior_off & bootstrap_off])
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "The median chain-bootstrap interval is a factor of %.2f wide against",
  "%.2f for the posterior interval; %d topics have a bootstrap interval",
  "off 1 against %d. Off 1 under the posterior but not under the",
  "bootstrap: %s. The reverse: %s. Raised with the bootstrap's interval",
  "in place of the posterior's: %s.\n"),
  exp(chain_width), exp(pooled_width), off_chain, off_one(pooled_lifts),
  or_none(lost), or_none(gained), or_none(raised_chain)))
top_rows <- head(arrange(chain, desc(lift)), 4)
knitr::kable(top_rows[, c("topic", "lift", "lift_q05", "lift_q95", "p_above",
                          "lift_chain_q05", "lift_chain_q95",
                          "p_chain_above")],
             digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("topic", "lift", "q05", "q95", "P(> 1)",
                           "chain q05", "chain q95", "chain P(> 1)"),
             caption = paste("The four largest lifts under the posterior",
                             "interval and the chain bootstrap"))
```

The dependence between the restorations matters more than the uncertainty
in $\phi$. The bootstrap interval of the median topic is a factor of
`r sprintf("%.2f", exp(chain_width))` wide against
`r sprintf("%.2f", exp(pooled_width))` for the posterior interval, and
`r length(lost)` topics whose posterior interval is off 1 have a bootstrap
interval that covers it. The topic with the largest lift,
*`r top_topic`*, keeps its interval off 1 and its probability under both;
the topics behind it are where the two readings part. Where the hard report
had only the bootstrap, the soft model has both, and the bootstrap is the
interval to quote for a claim about the walk as a whole, the posterior
interval for a claim about these `r imputations$n_docs[1]` documents.

# The lift along the walk

The pooled lift averages over `r pooled$chains` chains and all their
states. Whether the excess of *`r top_topic`* is a property of the walk as a
whole, or of a few chains or a stretch of steps, shows when the lift is
followed along the walk. Every fifth recorded state of every chain, one
every 50 steps, is sampled again under the mean $\phi$ and the LDA's mean
$\alpha$ (`scripts/soft_trajectory.py`, `slurm/soft_trajectory.slurm`, into
`results/soft/trajectory/`). The topic's posterior mean share, averaged over
a moving window of 1,000 steps, is divided by Sophocles' mean share under
the same plug-in model (`results/soft/mean_alpha_lda`); the dotted line is
the plug-in lift of all the chains together.

```{r trajectory_sets}
trajectory_path <- file.path(dirname(results_dir), "trajectory",
                             "trajectory.csv")
plugin_dir <- file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_lda")
trajectory_done <- file.exists(trajectory_path) &&
  file.exists(file.path(plugin_dir, "profiles.csv"))
```

```{r trajectory_missing, results = "asis", echo = FALSE, eval = !trajectory_done}
cat("The states along the walk have not been sampled yet: missing",
    trajectory_path, "\n")
```

```{r trajectory_read, eval = trajectory_done}
trajectory <- read.csv(trajectory_path, check.names = FALSE,
                       encoding = "UTF-8")
# Chain numbers repeat between the rounds of starts, so a chain is named by
# its round and its number (counted from 1)
round_of <- c(chains_judge235_t4_spread = "first",
              chains_judge235_t4_spread2 = "second",
              chains_judge235_t4_topic4 = "topic")
trajectory$chain <- paste(round_of[trajectory$chain_set],
                          trajectory$chain + 1)
plugin_profiles <- read.csv(file.path(plugin_dir, "profiles.csv"),
                            encoding = "UTF-8")
plugin_lift <- read.csv(file.path(plugin_dir, "comparisons.csv"),
                        encoding = "UTF-8")
sophocles_share <- plugin_profiles$mean[plugin_profiles$source == "sophocles" &
                                          plugin_profiles$topic == top_topic]
pooled_lift <- plugin_lift$lift[plugin_lift$comparison ==
                                  "imputations vs sophocles" &
                                  plugin_lift$topic == top_topic]
# a moving window of 20 states, 1,000 steps, within each chain
window <- 20
along <- trajectory %>%
  arrange(chain, step) %>%
  group_by(chain) %>%
  mutate(share = .data[[top_topic]],
         moving = if (n() >= window) {
           as.numeric(stats::filter(share, rep(1 / window, window), sides = 1))
         } else NA_real_,
         lift = moving / sophocles_share) %>%
  ungroup()
chain_lifts <- along %>%
  group_by(chain) %>%
  summarise(lift = mean(share) / sophocles_share)
```

```{r trajectory_plot, eval = trajectory_done, fig.height = 6.5}
ggplot(filter(along, !is.na(lift)), aes(x = step / 1000, y = lift)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pooled_lift, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(colour = okabe_ito[["vermillion"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ chain, ncol = 6) +
  labs(x = "step of the walk (thousands)",
       y = paste("lift of", top_topic, "against Sophocles"))
```

```{r trajectory_summary, eval = trajectory_done, results = "asis"}
windows_above <- mean(along$lift > 1, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "Over its whole run, every chain's lift of %s lies between %.2f and %.2f",
  "(%d of %d chains above 1), and %.0f %% of the 1,000-step windows of all",
  "chains are above 1. The %d sampled states have a split R-hat above 1.01",
  "in %d fits and divergent transitions in %d.\n"),
  top_topic, min(chain_lifts$lift), max(chain_lifts$lift),
  sum(chain_lifts$lift > 1), nrow(chain_lifts), 100 * windows_above,
  nrow(trajectory), sum(trajectory$max_rhat > 1.01),
  sum(trajectory$divergences > 0)))
```

# The prior

The Stan program has one modelling choice of its own, the prior on
$\theta$, and the report takes the $\alpha$ the LDA estimated on the tragedy
corpus. With $K - 1 = 37$ free dimensions and some 30 to 40 lemmata per
document the prior is not nothing: it decides how much of a document's mass
a topic may hold on the strength of a single lemma, and the learned
$\alpha$ is a strong statement, below 1 on every seeded topic and between 4
and 9 on the four free ones. Three hand-chosen priors are run through the
same pipeline under the same mean $\phi$ (tasks 20 to 23 of
`slurm/soft_draws.slurm`, into `results/soft/mean_alpha_*`): the flat
$\mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1)$; $\mathrm{Dirichlet}(0.1)$, which favours
documents made of a few topics; and $\mathrm{Dirichlet}(2)$, which favours
even mixtures. The learned prior under the mean $\phi$ is the fourth run,
so that only the prior moves between them. What matters is whether the
lifts, the raised set and the order of the topics survive the change.

```{r prior_sets}
prior_dirs <- c("learned" = file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_lda"),
                "1" = file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_1"),
                "0.1" = file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_0.1"),
                "2" = file.path(dirname(results_dir), "mean_alpha_2"))
prior_done <- file.exists(file.path(prior_dirs, "comparisons.csv"))
```

```{r prior_missing, results = "asis", echo = FALSE, eval = !all(prior_done)}
cat("The prior check has not been run yet: missing",
    paste(prior_dirs[!prior_done], collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r prior_read, eval = all(prior_done)}
read_prior <- function(alpha) {
  dir <- prior_dirs[[alpha]]
  lifts <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "comparisons.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
  lifts <- filter(lifts, comparison == "imputations vs sophocles")
  lifts$alpha <- alpha
  means <- read.csv(file.path(dir, "profiles.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
  list(lifts = lifts,
       diagnostics = read.csv(gzfile(file.path(dir, "diagnostics.csv.gz"))),
       seeded_mass = sum(means$mean[means$source == "imputations"]))
}
priors <- lapply(names(prior_dirs), read_prior)
names(priors) <- names(prior_dirs)
prior_lifts <- bind_rows(lapply(priors, `[[`, "lifts"))
prior_lifts$alpha <- factor(prior_lifts$alpha, levels = names(prior_dirs))
learned <- filter(prior_lifts, alpha == "learned")
```

Stan's diagnostics under each prior, counted over the documents as above.
A prior with concentrations below 1 puts mass against the faces of the
simplex, where the sampler has a harder time; the two priors at or above 1
sample without a flag.

```{r prior_diagnostics, eval = all(prior_done)}
prior_diagnostics <- bind_rows(lapply(names(priors), function(alpha) {
  d <- priors[[alpha]]$diagnostics
  data.frame(alpha = alpha, documents = nrow(d),
             rhat_over_1.01 = sum(d$max_rhat > 1.01),
             ess_under_400 = sum(d$min_ess_bulk < 400),
             divergent = sum(d$divergences > 0),
             treedepth = sum(d$treedepth_hits > 0),
             worst_rhat = max(d$max_rhat),
             least_ess = min(d$min_ess_bulk),
             seconds = median(d$seconds))
}))
knitr::kable(prior_diagnostics, digits = 3,
             caption = "Stan's diagnostics under the four priors")
```

The lift of every seeded topic against Sophocles under the four priors,
with its 90 % interval, ordered by the lift under the learned prior.

```{r prior_plot, eval = all(prior_done), fig.height = 6}
prior_lifts$topic <- factor(prior_lifts$topic,
                            levels = learned$topic[order(learned$lift)])
prior_colours <- c("learned" = okabe_ito[["vermillion"]], "1" = "grey40",
                   "0.1" = okabe_ito[["orange"]], "2" = okabe_ito[["blue"]])
ggplot(prior_lifts, aes(x = lift, y = topic, colour = alpha)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lift_q05, xmax = lift_q95),
                  size = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.7)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = prior_colours,
                      labels = c("learned", "Dirichlet(1)", "Dirichlet(0.1)",
                                 "Dirichlet(2)"),
                      name = "prior on theta") +
  labs(x = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles (log scale)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r prior_summary, eval = all(prior_done), results = "asis"}
lift_under <- function(alpha) {
  rows <- filter(prior_lifts, alpha == !!alpha)
  rows$lift[match(learned$topic, rows$topic)]
}
wide <- data.frame(topic = learned$topic, learned = lift_under("learned"),
                   flat = lift_under("1"), sparse = lift_under("0.1"),
                   even = lift_under("2"))
wide <- arrange(wide, desc(learned))
raised_under <- function(alpha) {
  rows <- filter(prior_lifts, alpha == !!alpha, lift_q05 > 1)
  as.character(arrange(rows, desc(lift))$topic)
}
raised_sets <- lapply(names(prior_dirs), raised_under)
names(raised_sets) <- names(prior_dirs)
raised_all <- Reduce(intersect, raised_sets)
# the slope of a prior's log lifts on the learned prior's: 1 would mean the
# same lifts, 1/2 that every lift is square-rooted
slope <- function(column) {
  unname(coef(lm(log(column) ~ log(wide$learned)))[2])
}
slopes <- sapply(wide[, c("flat", "sparse", "even")], slope)
correlations <- sapply(wide[, c("flat", "sparse", "even")],
                       function(column) cor(log(column), log(wide$learned)))
seeded_mass <- sapply(priors, `[[`, "seeded_mass")
# the topics whose interval is off 1 under the learned prior: do they keep
# their side of 1 under the other priors?
learned_sorted <- learned[match(wide$topic, learned$topic), ]
settled <- learned_sorted$lift_q05 > 1 | learned_sorted$lift_q95 < 1
same_side <- function(column) {
  sum(((column > 1) == (wide$learned > 1))[settled])
}
sides <- sapply(wide[, c("flat", "sparse", "even")], same_side)
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "Raised (interval above 1) under the learned prior: %s; under",
  "Dirichlet(1): %s; under Dirichlet(0.1): %s; under Dirichlet(2): %s;",
  "under all four: %s.\n\n"),
  or_none(raised_sets[["learned"]]), or_none(raised_sets[["1"]]),
  or_none(raised_sets[["0.1"]]), or_none(raised_sets[["2"]]),
  or_none(raised_all)))
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "The correlation of the log lifts with the learned prior's is %.3f for",
  "Dirichlet(1), %.3f for Dirichlet(0.1) and %.3f for Dirichlet(2);",
  "regressing a prior's log lifts on the learned prior's gives slopes of",
  "%.2f, %.2f and %.2f. Of the %d topics whose interval is off 1 under",
  "the learned prior, %d, %d and %d keep their side of 1. The seeded",
  "topics hold %.0f %%, %.0f %%, %.0f %% and %.0f %% of the imputations'",
  "mean profile under the learned prior, 1, 0.1 and 2.\n\n"),
  correlations[["flat"]], correlations[["sparse"]], correlations[["even"]],
  slopes[["flat"]], slopes[["sparse"]], slopes[["even"]], sum(settled),
  sides[["flat"]], sides[["sparse"]], sides[["even"]],
  100 * seeded_mass[["learned"]], 100 * seeded_mass[["1"]],
  100 * seeded_mass[["0.1"]], 100 * seeded_mass[["2"]]))
knitr::kable(wide, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("topic", "learned", "Dirichlet(1)",
                           "Dirichlet(0.1)", "Dirichlet(2)"),
             caption = "Lift against Sophocles under the four priors")
```

Three things the four runs show. First, the prior sets the scale of the
lifts: every log lift is multiplied by about
`r sprintf("%.1f", slopes[["flat"]])` under the flat prior and by about
`r sprintf("%.1f", slopes[["even"]])` under Dirichlet(2), and by about
`r sprintf("%.1f", slopes[["sparse"]])` under Dirichlet(0.1). The reason is
shrinkage. A Dirichlet prior acts as $\sum_k \alpha_k$ pseudo-lemmata laid
on the topics in proportion to $\alpha$, against the
`r round(mean(imputations$n_lemmata))` or so real lemmata of a document:
`r K` pseudo-lemmata at the flat prior, `r 2 * K` at $\alpha = 2$,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 0.1 * K)` at $\alpha = 0.1$ and
`r sprintf("%.1f", sum(phi$alpha))` under the learned prior, of which only
`r sprintf("%.1f", sum(phi$alpha[1:H]))` fall on the seeded topics. Under
the flat prior the prior already weighs more than the document, both mean
profiles are pulled towards the uniform profile and their ratio towards 1;
the learned prior leaves each seeded topic almost nothing unless the
document's lemmata call for it, and the differences between the sets come
out in full. A fixed threshold on the lift would therefore be a statement
relative to the prior. The raised set is defined on order instead, by an
interval above 1, and it still moves with the prior, in the other
direction: the symmetric priors pull the lifts towards 1 but tighten the
intervals too, so that `r length(raised_sets[["1"]])` topics clear the
line under Dirichlet(1) and `r length(raised_sets[["2"]])` under
Dirichlet(2), most of them with lifts below 1.3, against
`r length(raised_sets[["learned"]])` under the learned prior. The topics
raised under every prior are `r or_none(raised_all)`.

Second, the learned prior is not a symmetric prior at some other scale. Its
log lifts correlate at `r sprintf("%.2f", correlations[["sparse"]])` with
Dirichlet(0.1)'s and at `r sprintf("%.2f", correlations[["flat"]])` with
the flat prior's, where the symmetric priors correlate with each other
above 0.95; of the `r sum(settled)` topics whose interval is off 1 under
the learned prior, `r sides[["flat"]]` keep their side of 1 under the flat
prior and `r sides[["sparse"]]` under Dirichlet(0.1). Topic by topic,
$\alpha_k$ runs from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(phi$alpha[1:H]))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(phi$alpha[1:H]))`, so a topic with a small
$\alpha_k$ is read as under the sparse prior and one with a large
$\alpha_k$ as under a prior nearer the flat one: the learned prior has
different ideas about which topics a thirty-lemma document can hold at
all, and it took them from Aeschylus and Euripides.

Third, the free topics. Under the learned prior the four free topics,
broad topics fitted without seeds, take
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - seeded_mass[["learned"]]))` % of the
imputations' mean profile, against
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (1 - seeded_mass[["1"]]))` % under the flat prior,
because their $\alpha_k$ are large: the LDA found that most of a tragic
window is best explained by them, and says so in its prior. The seeded
topics then share the remaining quarter, and their lifts are ratios of
small shares, which is one reason the learned prior's intervals are wider
and its sampling harder. The learned prior is kept for the report because
it is the prior under which $\phi$ was fitted, with the understanding that
its lifts are the largest of the four and its order of the topics is the
one that differs most from the symmetric priors' consensus; the sign of
nearly every well-determined lift, and the topic at the top, are the same
under all four.
